title_guess: Balance of payments: forex flows, current and capital account, double entry and BoP crisis
running_examples: oil barrel imported and paid for in dollars vs gears (manufactured goods) exported and paid for in dollars
list of foreign-currency dealings: goods, services, tourism, NRI remittances, FDI, FPI, external borrowing

best_moments.why: goods and dollars travel opposite ways around one loop between the globe and India: import = oil in, dollars out; export = gears out, dollars in
double entry made visible: a small debit|credit chalkboard under every account leaf, then black frames group the boards into current and capital totals
BoP plus/minus wired by green and red arrows into the forex vault; crisis = the vault cannot cover the minus

weak_moments.why: the kinds of foreign-currency dealings are a plain bullet list under the arrow; each could have been shown flowing into or out of the vault
a full tree of small labels and bullet items (services, incomes, transfers, FDI, FPI, loans); dense, text carries everything
current-account surplus and deficit are introduced as faded text labels with dotted pointers, no picture of what a surplus is

segments.teaches: importing means paying foreign currency out; exporting means receiving foreign currency in

elements.what: slowly spinning globe on the left
India silhouette on the right
red elbow arrow from world to India labelled import, with an oil barrel on it
red curved arrow from India back to the world with a dollar-note bundle, labelled payments (foreign currency)
green elbow arrow from India to the world labelled export, with a gears icon on it
green curved arrow from the world to India with a dollar-note bundle, labelled receipts (foreign currency)

segments.notes: the globe keeps rotating for the first ~2 minutes, which is why the events file shows one long 'big' change from 4 to 138 s; the loop closes in four beats: goods in, money out, goods out, money in
segments.idea: trade moves money across borders: buying from the world sends foreign currency out, selling to the world brings it in
segments.shown_as: a globe on the left and India on the right; a red elbow arrow carries an oil barrel from the world to India (import), then a curved red arrow carries a dollar bundle back from India to the world (payment); a green elbow arrow carries gears from India out to the world (export) and a curved green arrow brings dollars back to India (receipt), closing a loop
segments.example: oil imported and paid in dollars; manufactured goods (gears) exported for dollars

segments.teaches: every foreign-currency dealing with the world raises or lowers India's forex reserve: goods, services, tourism, NRI remittances, FDI, FPI, external borrowing

elements.what: same spinning globe
India silhouette
light-blue box with two dollar notes labelled foreign currency, riding on a two-headed arrow between globe and India
line from India up to a block of six locker doors labelled forex reserve
locker block (vault) for the forex reserve
green 'increase' and red 'decrease' hooks under the vault
bullet list under the arrow growing to seven kinds of dealings

segments.notes: the loop collapses into one two-way exchange box; bullets are added one per narration beat (about every 6-10 s)
segments.idea: many kinds of dealings with other countries move foreign currency and so push the forex reserve up or down
segments.shown_as: the import/export loop folds into one two-way arrow between globe and India with a blue box of dollar notes riding on it; a line runs from India up to a block of lockers named forex reserve, which forks into a green 'increase' and a red 'decrease' hook; then a bullet list of dealing types grows under the arrow one item at a time
segments.example: goods, services, tourism, NRI remittances, FDI, FPI, external borrowings

segments.teaches: the balance of payments is a statement of all economic and financial transactions with the world in one year

elements.what: 'economic & financial transactions' heading over the currency box
the bullet list folds away; the heading moves under the box with '[1 year]'
short down-arrow
document icon labelled statement / balance of payment [BoP]

segments.notes: nice 'summarise then name' move: a long list is replaced by one umbrella label, and the label becomes a document = the definition
segments.idea: put all those dealings for one year in one statement and you have the balance of payments
segments.shown_as: the bullet list folds away and one umbrella label (economic and financial transactions, one year) takes its place under the currency box; a down-arrow drops from it to a document icon named the BoP statement

segments.teaches: BoP has a current account and a capital account; the current account = visibles (goods, balance of trade) + invisibles (services, incomes/NFIA, transfers)

elements.what: BoP document icon at the top
green elbow arrows split BoP into dashed chips current account and capital account
current account splits into balance of invisibles and balance of visibles (= balance of trade, BoT)
BoT down-arrow to 'goods'
three light-blue bars (services, incomes [NFIA], transfers) on a dotted vertical guide, each with small example bullets

segments.notes: canvas clears at ~137 s; examples: software and consultancy for services, remittances for transfers
segments.idea: the BoP has two halves; the current half counts goods traded plus services, incomes and gifts/remittances
segments.shown_as: a BoP document icon on top; green elbow arrows branch it into two dashed chips (current account, capital account); the current chip branches again into visibles (balance of trade, then goods) and invisibles, where three blue bars (services, incomes, transfers) appear and each gets small example bullets

segments.teaches: the capital account = investments (FDI, FPI incl. depository receipts, external bonds issued by the government) + loans (external lending and borrowing)

elements.what: capital account branches into investments and loans
green-square bullets: three under investments, two under loans

segments.notes: the whole tree stays on screen; the narrator fills one branch at a time
segments.idea: the capital half counts money that comes or goes as investment or as loans
segments.shown_as: the second chip (capital account) branches into investments and loans; investments gets three small bullets (FDI, FPI, government bonds sold abroad) and loans gets two (lending abroad, borrowing abroad), completing a four-leaf tree

segments.teaches: each sub-account is kept by double-entry bookkeeping (debit minus, credit plus), so each nets to plus or minus; current items add to one total and capital items to another

elements.what: four small chalkboards each with a debit|credit T-chart (- / +), one under each leaf
'double entry bookkeeping' label with a curved arrow to the boards
down-arrow under each board ending in '+ive / -ive'
black frame around the two current-account boards, another around the two capital-account boards, each with its own +/- result

segments.notes: bullet lists swap for chalkboards at ~238 s; frames at ~279 and ~285 s
segments.idea: every account is a two-sided ledger, so each account and each half of the BoP ends up in plus or minus
segments.shown_as: the bullet lists vanish and a small chalkboard with a debit|credit T-chart drops under each of the four leaves; a curved arrow names them double-entry bookkeeping; a down-arrow under each board ends in '+ / -'; then one black frame closes around the two current boards and another around the two capital boards, each frame getting its own +/- result

segments.teaches: the current account ends in surplus (CAS) or deficit (CAD); together with the capital account it makes the overall BoP

elements.what: current account and capital account chips, each now with '+ive / -ive' beneath
green 'current account surplus (CAS)' and red 'current account deficit (CAD)' with dotted pointers from the + and - signs
one black frame around both accounts

segments.notes: the boards fold back into two chips; CAS/CAD labels fade out before the frame joins both accounts
segments.idea: a plus on the current account is a surplus, a minus is a deficit; both accounts together give the BoP
segments.shown_as: the four boards fold up into the two account chips, each carrying just '+ / -'; a dotted pointer from the plus names current account surplus and one from the minus names current account deficit; then a black frame closes around both accounts to show they add up to the BoP

segments.teaches: a positive BoP adds to forex reserves, a negative BoP draws them down; if reserves cannot cover a negative BoP it is a BoP crisis

elements.what: BoP document with '+ive' on a green patch and '-ive' on a red patch
forex-reserve locker block (vault) below
green elbow arrow from + down into the vault labelled increase; red elbow arrow from - labelled decrease
side note defining BoP crisis, behind a wavy divider; the term gets a blue underline

segments.notes: callback: the vault from the first minutes returns, closing the story arc
segments.idea: BoP plus fills the reserve vault, BoP minus empties it; an empty vault facing a minus is a crisis
segments.shown_as: the framed accounts shrink to one '+ / -' line under the BoP icon over the vault of lockers; a green elbow arrow runs from the plus side into the vault labelled increase and a red one from the minus side labelled decrease; a side note says that when the vault cannot cover the minus it is a BoP crisis, and the term gets underlined

segments.teaches: channel end card (next video / playlist), no teaching

segments.shown_as: canvas replaced by an end card with next-video and playlist panels
